RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 50

An all-male panel selecting a male candidate with less leadership experience over a more qualified female applicant may suggest implicit or systemic bias, though interview performance or specific school needs could also explain the outcome.

Whether to raise it depends on context and procedure. First, demand the overdue written justification. Check whether local public-sector employment rules require gender-balanced hiring panels; if so, raise it as a formal procedural breach. Otherwise, do not raise the panel's gender in isolation, as it can sound speculative. Instead, consult your union or an employment lawyer to determine if the credential discrepancy, lack of response, and panel composition together substantiate a formal grievance.
